```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = NA)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
```

This tutorial introduces to data augmentation with the package `housepi`.
We explain the process of associating augmented variable to individuals to then proceed with standard model generation and inference.

## Estimate Incubation Periods Distribution

For simplicity, we start testing data augmentation on a database which is not a household survey.
Instead we consider a simulated report documenting the days when a number of cases were exposed to infection and the days of symptom onset.

Assuming the incubation period to be described by a gamma distribution, we want to estimate the respective parameters augmenting the exposure and onset times, modeled as uniformly distributed in the reported ranges.
We associate a positive status to all individuals and we correct for right censoring modifying the maximum values as follows:

```{r}
data("delays", package = "housepi")
delays[["exposure_max"]] <- delays[["exposure_max"]] + 1 - 1e-4
delays[["onset_max"]] <- delays[["onset_max"]] + 1 - 1e-4
delays[["status"]] <- 1
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(delays))
```

We generate the model as showed in the [Walkthrough](walkthrough.html):

```{r}
# generate an instance of the household model class
hmc_1 <- housepi::HouseholdModelClass$new("eg-augm-incubation-from-delays")

# gamma distribution parameter definitions
hmc_1$add_param(name = "shape",
                prior = "unif", args = list(min = 0, max = 5),
                rule = "norm", rule_scale = 1)
hmc_1$add_param(name = "scale",
                prior = "unif", args = list(min = 0, max = 5),
                rule = "norm", rule_scale = 1)
```

### Build Augmented Variables

Similarly to parameter definitions, for augmented variables we provide a DataFrame or a file with the models and proposer rules needed for the Bayesian Monte Carlo.
However, augmented variable definitions are more delicate, since they can depend on database or parameters.
We state which value should be imported from the database by formatting the string with the value header: "*header_name*`@D`".
Here we associate to each individual an exposure and an onset time.

```{r}
# add 'exposure' time definition
hmc_1$add_augm(
  name = "exposure",
  value = "exposure_min@D",            # start from data value 'exposure_min'
  model = "unif",                      # associate a uniform model
  args = list(min = "exposure_min@D",  # within the range 'exposure_min'
              max = "exposure_max@D"), # and 'exposure_max'
  rule = "norm",                       # normal rule for the Monte Carlo
  rule_scale = 0.5                     # with std. dev. 0.5
)

# add 'onset' time definition
hmc_1$add_augm(
  name = "onset",
  value = "onset_max@D",
  model = "unif", args = list(min = "onset_min@D", max = "onset_max@D"),
  rule = "norm", rule_scale = 0.5
)
```

We run the inference and we extract the results

```{r}
hmc_1$infer(data = delays, n_steps = 100000, 
            n_burnin = 10000, thin = 10, 
            n_adapt = 2500, seed = 4349)
# Note: The warning tells us that our database has no demographic structure:
# it will be interpreted as single individuals living in separate households.

# collect the inference results
results_1 <- hmc_1$summarise_traces()
```

## Augment Onset Times

For a more realistic example, we use the template model "ex-augm-onset-single-intro", where surveys are conditioned on single introduction and follow the times of onset.
For simplicity the model assumes no asymptomatic cases.

```{r}
hmc_2 <- housepi::HouseholdModelClass$new("eg-augm-onset-single-intro")
```

This time we load the parameter definitions directly from the model template.

```{r}
# use example parameters associated to the templated model
hmc_2$template_param()

# export the data.frame with parameter definitions
par_2 <- hmc_2$export_param()
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(par_2)
```

We propose the following definitions for the augmented variable

```{r}
# associate defininitions from a list
aug_defs <- list(
  # add augmented variable definition 'onset_date'
  onset_date = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    model = "lnorm", args = list(meanlog = 4, sdlog = 0.5),
    max = 365
  ),
  # add augmented variable definition 'incub_period'
  incub_period = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    # assign arguments of incubation period from parameter definitions
    model = "gamma", args = list(shape = "inc_shape@P",
                                 scale = "inc_scale@P"),
    max = 14
  )
)
hmc_2$load_augm_list(aug_defs, append = FALSE)

# use inferred values from first example as constant parameters
aug_defs <- list(
  inc_shap = list(value = results_1["shape", "Mean"]),
  inc_scale = list(value = results_1["scale", "Mean"])
)
hmc_2$load_augm_list(aug_defs, append = TRUE)
```

### Simulate an Outbreak

We run a simulation with the method `simulate`.

```{r}
# override status of the dataset according to simulation
data("survey", package = "housepi")
hmc_2$simulate(data = survey, seed = 3731)

# show a summary of the current database
hmc_2$data_summary()
```

In addition to the final status, the simulation associates the values of the augmented variables: the incubation period and the onset time.
This simulation, as all templated models, do not simulate a sampling process.

```{r}
# remove incubation period from simulated database
df <- subset(hmc_2$export_data(), select = -c(incub_period))

# change all onsets after 9 PM to next day
is_infec <- df$status == 1
df[is_infec, "onset_date"] <- sapply(
  df[is_infec, "onset_date"],
  function(x) if ((x %% 1) > 0.875) ceiling(x) else floor(x)
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(df))
```

### Validate the Simulation

We can check that inference returns the parameters used for the simulation.

```{r}
# add new definitions
new_augm_defs <- list(
  # add 'onset_date' definition
  onset_date = list(
    value = "onset_date@D",
    rule = "norm", rule_scale = 0.25,
    rule_from = "onset_date@D"
  ),
  # add 'incub_period' definition
  incub_period = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    model = "gamma", args = list(shape = "inc_shape@P",
                                 scale = "inc_scale@P"),
    rule = "gibbs", max = 14
  )
)

# drop previous definitions and load new from list
hmc_2$load_augm_list(new_augm_defs, append = FALSE)

# perform the inference
# note: NA onset dates of healthy individuals will raise a warning
hmc_2$infer(data = df, n_steps = 10000, n_burnin = 1000, thin = 10,
            n_chains = 3, n_adapt = 2000, seed = 3413, progress = FALSE)
```

```{r, fig.align = 'center'}
# plot the traces of all chains 
lattice::xyplot(hmc$export_traces())
```

```{r}
# collect the results
results_2 <- hmc_2$summarise_traces()

# compare results to parameter values used for inference
imask <- par_2["infer"] == TRUE
inames <- par_2[imask, "name"]
results_2[inames, "Simul"] <- par_2[imask, "value"]
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(results_2, digits = 3)
```

### Model Comparison

We can estimate the model evidence (or marginal loglikelihood) with the method of the power posteriors:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# return the estimate of the model evidence
hmc_2$evidence(n_rungs = 30)
```
